facts.text: Mass is how much matter a machine contains, payload is the load the machine carries, and gross vehicle weight rating (GVWR) is the manufacturer's allowed maximum total of machine plus load.
facts.quote: Mass is how much matter a machine contains, payload is the load it carries, and the gross vehicle weight rating (GVWR) is the maximum total of machine plus load that the manufacturer allows.

facts.text: Payload on heavy machines can exceed the mass of the empty machine.
facts.quote: On heavy machines the payload can exceed the empty machine

facts.text: The Volvo A60 articulated hauler has an empty mass of about 44 t and a gross mass of about 99 t.
facts.quote: a Volvo A60 articulated hauler at about 44 t empty and 99 t gross

facts.text: The Caterpillar 797F mining truck has a gross mass of about 624 t with a 363 t payload.
facts.quote: a Caterpillar 797F mining truck at about 624 t gross with a 363 t payload [Chapter 8]

facts.text: A loaded machine can be twice as heavy as an empty machine.
facts.quote: A loaded machine can be twice as heavy as an empty one

facts.text: A loaded machine's center of gravity sits higher and further back than that of the empty machine.
facts.quote: A loaded machine can be twice as heavy as an empty one, and its center of gravity (the point where its mass balances) sits higher and further back.

facts.text: Real machines have limited brake force and heat absorption capacity, so a heavier machine with the same brakes decelerates less.
facts.quote: Brakes produce only a limited force and absorb only so much heat, so a heavier machine with the same brakes decelerates less.

facts.text: Payload shifts load between the axles and changes how much braking force each wheel or track can transmit.
facts.quote: Payload also shifts load between the axles, changes how much braking force each wheel or track can transmit

facts.text: Payload brings a machine closer to tipping.
facts.quote: Payload also shifts load between the axles, changes how much braking force each wheel or track can transmit, and brings the machine closer to tipping [Chapter 8].

facts.text: ISO 3450 tests a machine in the configuration having the most adverse effect on braking, with dumpers at maximum payload.
facts.quote: The brake standard ISO 3450 therefore tests a machine in the configuration "having the most adverse effect on braking", with dumpers at maximum payload [Chapter 8].

facts.text: The automatic brake must know the machine's loading or assume the worst loading, because payload changes stopping distance and whether hard braking is safe.
facts.quote: The automatic brake must know, or assume the worst about, how heavily the machine is loaded, because payload changes both how far the machine travels before it stops and whether hard braking is safe.

facts.text: A single vehicle mass is an inadequate description for the stopping model; payload must be a variable in that model.
facts.quote: The booklet concludes that "one vehicle mass" is an inadequate description, that payload must be a variable in the stopping model

facts.text: Machines whose mass changes substantially belong in a different model family from machines of nearly fixed mass.
facts.quote: machines whose mass changes a lot belong in a different model family from machines of nearly fixed mass [Chapter 8]
